cues.en: So, good afternoon everybody. Hope you've enjoyed the first day of LeadDev. I know I certainly have. It's quite the honor to be able to share this stage with so many amazing speakers.
cues.zh: 大家下午好。希望你们喜欢 LeadDev 的第一天。我知道我肯定很喜欢。能在这个舞台上与这么多出色的演讲者同台，真是莫大的荣幸。

cues.en: So thank you to the organizers and to Mary,
cues.zh: 感谢组织者和 Mary，

cues.en: the committee chair and all the speakers who have presented to us today.
cues.zh: 委员会主席，以及今天为我们演讲的所有演讲者。

cues.en: Like Mary said, name is Nicholas Means. I'm VP of Engineering at WellMatch Health. I work with a lot of really smart people to help make The US healthcare system better. If you wanna know more about what I do, come talk to me because with a British audience, it's gonna be a conversation. It's not not something I I can explain from stage.
cues.zh: 就像 Mary 说的，我叫 Nicholas Means。我是 WellMatch Health 的工程副总裁。我与许多非常聪明的人共事，帮助改善美国医疗保健系统。如果你想更了解我的工作，来找我聊聊吧，因为面对英国听众，这会是一场对话。这不是我在台上能解释清楚的事。

cues.en: But another thing you need to know about me is that I am a student of plane crashes.
cues.zh: 但关于我，你还需要知道的另一件事是，我是飞机坠毁事故的研究者。

cues.en: I know that's a weird thing to say, but if you wanna if you wanna nerd snipe me, come up to me and ask me about a plane crash that I can't tell you the details about right off the top of my head.
cues.zh: 我知道这么说很奇怪，但如果你想引起我的兴趣，来找我聊一起我无法立刻说清细节的飞机坠毁事故吧。

cues.en: Joe, one of the members of the conference staff did this to me last night at the speakers dinner.
cues.zh: Joe，会议工作人员之一，昨晚在演讲者晚宴上就这么对我做了。

cues.en: And so instead of going home to the hotel and rehearsing my talk,
cues.zh: 于是我并没有回酒店排练演讲，

cues.en: I went back and looked up the details of a British Airways incident where the windscreen got sucked out of an airplane and the pilot got sucked out halfway.
cues.zh: 而是回去查了一起英国航空事故的细节，那架飞机的挡风玻璃被吸了出去，飞行员被吸出去一半。

cues.en: And still they managed to land and everybody survived.
cues.zh: 但他们仍然成功着陆，所有人都活了下来。

cues.en: It was British Airways flight
cues.zh: 那是英国航空

cues.en: five thousand three and ninety if you want go look it up yourself.
cues.zh: 5390 号航班，如果你想自己去查的话。

cues.en: But it's not it's not the morbidity of plane crashes or the spectacle that fascinates me. It's the dynamics of what happens in the cockpit. What the flight crew goes through
cues.zh: 但吸引我的并不是空难的致死率，也不是那种视觉奇观。而是驾驶舱里发生的事情的动态过程。是机组人员所经历的一切What the flight crew goes through

cues.en: from when an incident starts to when the plane gets to the ground, one way or the other.
cues.zh: 从突发状况发生到飞机落地，不管是以哪种方式。

cues.en: There's two kinds of ways this go. There's some flight crews that take tiny incidents
cues.zh:
这种情况大致有两种。有些机组人员会把小事故
@@O
take tiny incidents and they treat them as sort of major anomalies.

cues.en: and through poor reactions or poor decisions, take tiny system faults and make them into giant disasters.
cues.zh: 由于反应不当或决策失误，将微小的系统故障演变成巨大的灾难。

cues.en: Then there's other incidents where flight crews take giant problems, insurmountable obstacles,
cues.zh: 也有一些事故中，机组人员面对巨大的难题和看似不可逾越的障碍，

cues.en: and somehow manage to eke out a better outcome than they ought to be able to.
cues.zh: 而且不知何故，它们设法挤出了比本应达到的更好的结果。

cues.en: And the story I wanna tell you today is the story of one of the latter.
cues.zh: 今天我想讲的是后一类中的一个故事。

cues.en: It's the story of a flight crew who takes a plane
cues.zh: 这是一个关于机组人员驾驶飞机的故事

cues.en: that's struck with almost insurmountable peril
cues.zh: 那几乎充满了难以逾越的危险

cues.en: and manages to save more than half the people on board.
cues.zh: 并成功救下了船上过半的人。

cues.en: It's what I think is one of the most fascinating plane crashes
cues.zh: 我认为这是最引人入胜的坠机事件之一

cues.en: in aviation history, the story of United two thirty two.
cues.zh: 在航空史上，联合航空232号班机的故事。
所以是1989年7月19日

cues.en: was an absolutely
cues.zh: 曾经是一个绝对的

cues.en: beautiful day in Denver, Colorado.
cues.zh: 科罗拉多州丹佛市天气晴朗。

cues.en: The high was summer in the mid eighties, scattered clouds.
cues.zh: 那是一年中盛夏的八月中旬，零星点缀着几朵白云。

cues.en: There was a wonderful breeze blowing in off the front range of the Rocky Mountains.
cues.zh: 落基山脉前麓吹来一阵惬意的微风。

cues.en: It was the kind of day if you've ever been to Denver in the summer, it's the kind of day that just begs you to go outside and do something. Go for a hike. Play around a golf.
cues.zh: 如果你去过夏天的 Denver，就知道那种天气特别适合出门做点什么。去徒步，或者打几洞高尔夫。

cues.en: It was also a wonderful day for flying at Denver Stapleton International Airport.
cues.zh: 那天也是丹佛斯台普顿国际机场非常适合飞行的日子。

cues.en: Planes were leaving on time.
cues.zh: 飞机准点起飞。

cues.en: Everything was running smoothly.
cues.zh: 一切都运行得很顺利。

cues.en: And at about
cues.zh: 大约在

cues.en: 10:30 or eleven in the morning, the first of the 285
cues.zh: 上午十点半或十一点，最终将登上联合航空232号航班的285名

cues.en: passengers and 11 crew members that would eventually be on board United flight two thirty two started arriving at the gate.
cues.zh: 乘客和11名机组人员中的第一批人开始抵达登机口。

cues.en: Their flight that day would take them from Denver, Stapleton Airport to Chicago O'Hare,
cues.zh: 他们当天的航班将把他们从丹佛斯台普顿机场带到芝加哥奥黑尔，

cues.en: or so they thought when they crossed the jet bridge.
cues.zh: 至少他们走过登机廊桥时是这么想的。

cues.en: If you were in the boarding lounge that day, you would have seen something like this through the window. It's a bit of an unfamiliar sight to a modern traveler.
cues.zh: 如果你那天在候机室里，透过窗户你会看到这样的景象。对现代旅客来说，这场景有点陌生。

cues.en: Back in these days, it was forbidden for planes to fly extended distances
cues.zh: 在那个年代，飞机被禁止只靠两台发动机

cues.en: with only two engines. They had to have more redundancy than that, so airlines invested heavily in what they called trijets.
cues.zh: 进行长距离飞行。它们必须有更多的冗余，所以航空公司大力投资于他们所谓的“三发客机”。

cues.en: Planes
cues.zh: 也就是

cues.en: that had two engines under the wings and one mounted through the tail.
cues.zh: 机翼下有两台发动机、尾部还装有一台的飞机。

cues.en: And that's what you would been getting on this day. Specifically,
cues.zh: 而这就是你那天要登上的飞机。具体来说，

cues.en: a DC 10
cues.zh: 是一架DC-10

cues.en: series 10 aircraft,
cues.zh: 系列10型飞机，

cues.en: tail registration number November 1819 uniform. That picture is the actual plane you would have been getting on that day.
cues.zh: 尾号注册号为November 1819 uniform。那张照片就是你们那天实际要登上的飞机。

cues.en: It was an old but proud plane.
cues.zh: 它是一架老旧但值得骄傲的飞机。

cues.en: It was delivered to United in 1971
cues.zh: 它于1971年交付给联合航空，

cues.en: and had been in service since then for about eighteen years.
cues.zh: 此后服役了大约十八年。

cues.en: Now eighteen years seems kinda old for an airliner, but it's really not. United would actually fly their DC 10 flight fleet well into its thirties, and you can still see these planes around the world today carrying packages and FedEx delivery. A lot of them are still operating.
cues.zh: 十八年对一架客机来说似乎有点老了，但其实并不是。联合航空实际上会把他们的DC-10机队飞到三十多年，而且你今天仍然能在世界各地看到这些飞机运送包裹和FedEx快递。其中很多仍在运营。

cues.en: As you got onboard, you would have seen something like this.
cues.zh: 登机后，你会看到这样的情况。

cues.en: If you've been onboard a Boeing triple seven recently,
cues.zh: 如果你最近坐过波音777，

cues.en: this cabin is just a little bit wider than that. It was a wide and roomy cabin. It was a quiet plane.
cues.zh: 这个客舱比那个稍宽一些。它宽敞舒适，飞行安静。

cues.en: And pilots loved to fly it. They referred to it as the Cadillac Fleetwood of the skies because it was such a comfortable ride.
cues.zh: 飞行员很喜欢驾驶它，称它为天空中的凯迪拉克Fleetwood，因为乘坐体验非常舒适。

cues.en: And the three engines gave it way more power than it needed so they loved,
cues.zh: 三台发动机提供的动力远超所需，所以他们很喜欢，

cues.en: loved being able to put their hand in the throttles and push them forward for takeoff
cues.zh: 喜欢在起飞时手握油门推杆向前推

cues.en: and let the power of that plane slam them back in their seats as they took the skies.
cues.zh: 让飞机的动力把他们猛推回座位，冲向天空。

cues.en: Around 02:10 in the afternoon that day,
cues.zh: 那天下午大约2点10分，

cues.en: that's exactly what happened.
cues.zh: 正是如此。

cues.en: It was a textbook takeoff out of Denver Stapleton.
cues.zh: 从丹佛Stapleton机场起飞堪称教科书级别。

cues.en: They turned east northeast out of the airport towards Chicago,
cues.zh: 他们从机场转向东北偏东，飞往芝加哥，

cues.en: and if you'd been in the cabin at that point, you'd have smelled chicken strips.
cues.zh: 如果那时你在客舱里，会闻到鸡肉条的味道。

cues.en: United was running a promotion that summer. They called their picnic lunch.
cues.zh: 那年夏天美联航在搞促销，他们称之为野餐午餐。

cues.en: So if you were flying at lunchtime, they would bring you a little basket covered in red white checked paper with picnic lunch in it. And that day it happened to be chicken strips, a few Oreos, and a cup full of cherries.
cues.zh: 所以如果你在午餐时间飞行，他们会给你一个小篮子，盖着红白格子纸，里面装着野餐午餐。那天碰巧是鸡肉条、几块奥利奥和一杯樱桃。

cues.en: Well about an hour into the flight,
cues.zh: 飞行大约一小时后，

cues.en: most people had finished their lunches.
cues.zh: 大多数人都吃完了午餐。

cues.en: The flight crew was beginning to pick up from lunch.
cues.zh: 机组人员开始收拾午餐。

cues.en: Jim McKay, the legendary American sportscaster from ABC's wide world of sports was about twenty minutes into explaining the history of horse racing in the in flight movie, Jewels of the Triple Crown. Sounds thrilling, know.
cues.zh: ABC《体育世界》传奇美国体育播音员Jim McKay，在机上电影《三冠王珍宝》中讲解赛马历史大约二十分钟了。听起来很刺激，是吧。

cues.en: And about that point,
cues.zh: 关于这一点，

cues.en: what had become... What had been a completely normal flight up until then suddenly changed.
cues.zh: 原本一切正常的一趟航班，直到那时突然发生了变化。

cues.en: There was a tremendous bang at the back of the airplane.
cues.zh: 飞机尾部传来一声巨响。

cues.en: Passengers thought maybe a bomb had gone off.
cues.zh: 乘客们以为可能是炸弹爆炸了。

cues.en: The flight crew across the plane hit the deck and grabbed the nearest armrest afraid that what they had heard was an explosive decompression and that they might be sucked out of the plane.
cues.zh: 机组人员立刻扑倒在地，抓紧最近的扶手，生怕刚才听到的是爆炸性减压，自己会被吸出机舱。

cues.en: Well it was neither of those things. What had actually happened is the fan disc in the number two engine,
cues.zh: 嗯，其实都不是。真正发生的情况是，2号发动机的风扇盘——

cues.en: the tail mounted engine,
cues.zh: 也就是安装在尾部的发动机，

cues.en: had exploded.
cues.zh: 爆炸了。

cues.en: On the flight deck, they had just finished their lunches when they heard this explosion.
cues.zh: 在驾驶舱里，机组人员刚吃完午饭就听到了这次爆炸。

cues.en: First officer Bill Records, who would've been sitting in that seat on your right there, immediately yells, I've got it. Lunges forward, grabs the yoke, disables the autopilot,
cues.zh: 副驾驶Bill Records（也就是你们右边那个座位上的人）立刻大喊：“我来控制！”他向前一冲，抓住驾驶杆，关闭了自动驾驶，

cues.en: and starts flying the plane by hand.
cues.zh: 开始手动驾驶飞机。

cues.en: Dudley Dvorak, the flight engineer who would have been sitting at that control console right there on the right,
cues.zh: 飞行工程师Dudley Dvorak（当时坐在右边那个控制台旁），

cues.en: starts checking his gauges and immediately notices that the number two engine has failed.
cues.zh: 开始检查仪表，并立刻发现2号发动机已经失效。

cues.en: So he radios Minneapolis St. Paul Air Control Center,
cues.zh: 于是他通过无线电联系明尼阿波利斯-圣保罗空中管制中心，

cues.en: not to declare an emergency,
cues.zh: 倒不是为了宣布紧急状态，

cues.en: but just ask for a clearance to lower altitude.
cues.zh: 只是请求批准降低飞行高度。

cues.en: Because on a DC 10, I mentioned the redundancy of the three engines. It actually wasn't that big a deal to lose an engine. With the reliability of these engines built in the seventies and eighties, losing an engine wasn't all that uncommon.
cues.zh: 因为在一架DC-10上，我提到过三台发动机的冗余设计。其实失去一台发动机并不是什么大事。考虑到七八十年代制造的这些发动机的可靠性，少了一台发动机其实并不那么罕见。

cues.en: So standard procedure was just to request a lower altitude, slow down a little bit, and continue on to your destination.
cues.zh: 所以标准程序就是请求降低高度，稍微减速，然后继续飞往目的地。

cues.en: And that's exactly what they intended to do.
cues.zh: 他们也正打算这么做。

cues.en: About this point, Captain Al Haynes, who was sitting in the pilot seat that day, asks for the engine shutdown checklist from from flight engineer Dudley Dvorak.
cues.zh: 大约就在这时，当天坐在驾驶座上的机长 Al Haynes 向飞行工程师 Dudley Dvorak 要发动机关闭检查单。

cues.en: Now Captain Haynes at this point was primarily concerned with making sure that whatever happened to this number two engine didn't escalate into a bigger crisis. When an engine failed, it's possible that it could be catching on fire or there could be physical damage. And he wanted to avoid making the situation any worse. So he asked WDvorak to start in on the checklist.
cues.zh: 此时 Haynes 机长主要关心的是，确保2号发动机无论出了什么状况，都不会升级成更大的危机。发动机失效时，可能会起火，也可能有物理损伤。他想避免让情况进一步恶化。于是他让 Dvorak 开始执行检查单。

cues.en: The first thing on the checklist
cues.zh: 检查单上的第一项

cues.en: was to close the number two
cues.zh: 是关闭2号

cues.en: throttle.
cues.zh: 油门。

cues.en: And so Captain Haynes tried to do that and he couldn't.
cues.zh: 于是 Haynes 机长试着去做，但做不到。

cues.en: It wouldn't budge. The throttle was stuck.
cues.zh: 它纹丝不动。油门卡住了。

cues.en: So they moved on to the second step of the checklist.
cues.zh: 于是他们继续看检查单的第二步。

cues.en: The second step was to shut off the fuel shutoff to this engine. They tried that as well.
cues.zh: 第二步是关闭这台发动机的燃油切断开关。他们也试了。

cues.en: Wouldn't budge.
cues.zh: 还是纹丝不动。

cues.en: And it was at this point that they finally understood
cues.zh: 就在这时，他们终于明白

cues.en: that something more than a routine engine failure had befallen their beautiful plane that day.
cues.zh: 那天降临到这架漂亮飞机上的，不只是普通的发动机失效。

cues.en: The thing you need to know about the DC 10 is that the throttle and the fuel shutoff are both physically coupled to the engine via a steel cable. If you think about how a bicycle brake works, it's the same theory.
cues.zh: 关于 DC-10，你需要知道的是，油门和燃油切断开关都通过一根钢缆与发动机物理连接。想想自行车刹车的工作原理，道理是一样的。

cues.en: So the fact that both of those controls were jammed
cues.zh: 所以，两个操纵装置都卡死这一事实

cues.en: told the flight crew that there must be some significant
cues.zh: 告诉机组人员，飞机肯定遭受了严重的

cues.en: physical damage to the aircraft.
cues.zh: 物理损坏。

cues.en: So Haynes and Dvorak were trying to figure out what to do next when Bill Records from the copilot seat shouts,
cues.zh: 于是 Haynes 和 Dvorak 正在想办法应对接下来该怎么办，这时副驾驶座上的 Bill Records 喊道：

cues.en: Al,
cues.zh: Al，

cues.en: I can't control the plane.
cues.zh: 我控制不了飞机。

cues.en: Which is a terrifying thing to hear.
cues.zh: 这句话听起来让人毛骨悚然。

cues.en: So Captain Haynes looks over and Bill Records,
cues.zh: 于是 Haynes 机长看过去，只见 Bill Records

cues.en: with his arms as tense as they could be, has the yoke all the way back,
cues.zh: 双臂绷得紧紧的，把驾驶盘一直拉到最后，

cues.en: all the way to the left.
cues.zh: 并且一直打到最左边。

cues.en: And there's two things about this that terrify him. The first thing is you would never give an aircraft that kind of input at cruise speed.
cues.zh: 这件事有两点让他感到恐惧。首先，飞机在巡航速度下，绝不能做出这种幅度的操纵。

cues.en: It'd be like driving down the highway at 85 miles an hour and suddenly jerking the steering wheel all the way to the left. You would lose control of the plane if you did that.
cues.zh: 这就像以每小时 85 英里的速度在高速公路上行驶时，突然把方向盘猛打到最左边。那样做会让飞机失去控制。

cues.en: But even more terrifying than that,
cues.zh: 但更可怕的是，

cues.en: despite the fact that
cues.zh: 尽管

cues.en: records had the yoke all the way back, which would command the plane to go up, and all the way to the left, which would command the plane to turn left,
cues.zh: Records 已经把驾驶盘一直拉到底，这会让飞机上升，同时又一直打到最左边，这会让飞机向左转，

cues.en: it was doing the exact opposite.
cues.zh: 飞机却做出了完全相反的动作。

cues.en: It was descending
cues.zh: 它正在下降

cues.en: and rolling to the right.
cues.zh: 并向右滚转。

cues.en: So at this point, Captain Haynes yells, I've got it. And he takes the controls from Bill Records and tries to see if he can have any effect on the control surfaces of the plane.
cues.zh: 这时，Haynes 机长大喊：“我来接管。”他从 Bill Records 手中接过操纵装置，试着看看自己能否对飞机的操纵面产生任何影响。

cues.en: Meanwhile, flight engineer Dudley Dvorak is still studying his gauges trying to figure out exactly what's happened to his beautiful plane.
cues.zh: 与此同时，飞行工程师 Dudley Dvorak 仍在研究仪表，努力弄清楚他那架漂亮的飞机究竟出了什么问题。

cues.en: When something catches his attention, he glances up from his gauges momentarily
cues.zh: 当有东西引起他的注意时，他会短暂地从仪表上抬眼一瞥

cues.en: out the windscreen of the aircraft
cues.zh: 透过飞机的挡风玻璃

cues.en: and immediately yells, we're rolling.
cues.zh: 立刻大喊，我们在侧倾。

cues.en: At this point the plane is about 38 degrees of bank, which is pretty steep for a commercial plane. It'd be pretty uncomfortable if you were back in the passenger cabin.
cues.zh: 此时飞机大约有38度的侧倾角，对商用客机来说相当陡。如果你在后方客舱里，会感到非常不适。

cues.en: And immediately to an instinct that he still doesn't understand to this day,
cues.zh: 而凭着一种至今他自己都不理解的直觉，

cues.en: Captain Haynes swats the number one throttle closed,
cues.zh: Haynes机长一把将一号油门收到底，

cues.en: opens the number three throttle all the way to the firewall wide open.

cues.en: It's actually one of the default flight modes of an aircraft with no flight control surfaces.
cues.zh: 实际上，这是没有飞行控制面的飞机默认飞行模式之一。

cues.en: What happens is a plane without flight control surfaces will immediately dip into a dive,
cues.zh: 情况是这样的：没有飞行控制面的飞机会立刻进入俯冲，

cues.en: and slowly it'll build airspeed over the wings which will build lift,

cues.en: until it loses airspeed, until it loses lift on the wings and start to descend again. The plane is trying to find equilibrium between the lift on the wings and the gravity acting on the plane.
cues.zh: 直到失去空速、失去机翼升力，然后再次开始下降。飞机在试图寻找机翼升力与作用在飞机上的重力之间的平衡。

cues.zh: 你可以凭借你声音所承载的权威有效地引导团队，但这是一把双刃剑。你也可能创造出这样一种局面：你是唯一引导团队的声音，其他人都不敢发表意见。

cues.en: This is especially true
cues.zh: 这一点尤其适用于

cues.en: with new engineers.
cues.zh: 新工程师。

cues.en: You need to give new engineers space to develop their identity in software, to assert
cues.zh: 你需要给新工程师空间，让他们在软件领域发展自己的身份认同，确立

cues.en: their growing authority and to make the mistakes they need to make to learn and grow. If there's only one dominant voice and it's constantly correcting new engineers on the team, they're never going to make the mistakes that they need to make in order to learn the lessons they have to learn.
cues.zh: 他们日益增长的专业权威，并犯下他们需要犯的错误来学习和成长。如果只有一个主导性声音，而且它不断纠正团队中的新工程师，他们就永远无法犯下那些为了学到必须学到的教训而需要犯的错误。

cues.en: It's also essential
cues.zh: 这也是至关重要的

cues.en: if you're building a diverse team and you absolutely should be because of the diversity of perspective and expertise that it brings to your team.
cues.zh: 如果你正在组建一个多元化的团队，而且你绝对应该这样做，因为这能为团队带来多样化的视角和专业知识。

cues.en: But if you allow dominant voices to take over the conversation of your teams,
cues.zh: 但如果你允许强势的声音主导团队的对话，

cues.en: you'll find it very hard to attract and keep diverse talent on your team.
cues.zh: 你会发现很难在团队中吸引并留住多元化的人才。

cues.en: Because voices that are used to being marginalized
cues.zh: 因为那些习惯被边缘化的声音

cues.en: will pick up on that pattern very quickly.
cues.zh: 会非常敏锐地察觉到这种模式。

cues.en: And they won't hang around to give you the benefit of the doubt and see how it's going to turn
cues.zh: 他们不会留下来给你benefit of the doubt（给予信任）去观察事情会如何发展。

cues.en: So if you want to build diversity on your teams, you have to make sure that everybody in your team has a voice. You have to cultivate that team culture.
cues.zh: 所以，如果你想在团队中建立多元化，就必须确保团队中的每个人都有发言权。你必须培养这样的团队文化。

cues.en: One of the interesting things about cockpit resource management is that the captain is still the captain.
cues.zh: 关于驾驶舱资源管理，有一件很有趣的事，那就是机长依然是机长。

cues.en: Every decision that's made in the cockpit still comes down to him.
cues.zh: 驾驶舱里做出的每一个决定，最终仍然取决于他。

cues.en: So as a team lead, you do still have authority.
cues.zh: 所以作为团队负责人，你确实依然拥有权威。

cues.en: But in cockpit resource management, the captain's job is to ensure that he uses his authority to make sure that every voice on the cockpit is heard. Everybody has input.
cues.zh: 但在驾驶舱资源管理中，机长的职责是确保他利用自己的权威，让驾驶舱里的每一个声音都被听到。每个人都有输入。

cues.en: That he's heard every idea available.
cues.zh: 确保他听取了所有可行的想法。

cues.en: Without that,
cues.zh: 如果没有这一点，

cues.en: it's really doubtful that this crew could have gotten this outcome out of United flight two thirty two.
cues.zh: 这个机组人员能否让联合航空232号航班取得这样的结果，真的很成问题。

cues.en: They wouldn't have made it to Sioux City Airport.
cues.zh: 他们根本到不了苏城机场。

cues.en: They wouldn't have gotten to the first responders who got every survivor to the hospital in under forty five minutes.
cues.zh: 他们也无法联系到第一响应者，从而在45分钟内将每一位幸存者送往医院。

cues.en: They would have been crashed in the middle of a cornfield somewhere in Iowa and it would have taken the response much longer. And the outcome that they would have been far different.
cues.zh: 他们会在爱荷华州某处的玉米地里坠毁，响应时间也会长得多。而且结果会截然不同。

cues.en: So remember that software is a team sport. Building software takes technical skill,
cues.zh: 所以请记住，软件开发是一项团队运动。构建软件需要技术能力，

cues.en: but building the right software
cues.zh: 但构建正确的软件

cues.en: takes human interaction and lots of it. So make sure you're building that kind of culture on your team. A lot of our teams tend to look like those flight crews that brought planes down.
cues.zh: 需要人与人之间的互动，而且是大量的互动。所以一定要在你的团队中建立这种文化。我们很多团队往往就像那些把飞机弄坠毁的机组人员。

cues.en: Let's work together
cues.zh: 让我们携手合作

cues.en: to look more like the crew of flight two thirty two.
cues.zh: 让我们的团队更像二三二航班的机组。

cues.en: If we do that, if we focus
cues.zh: 如果我们做到这一点，如果我们专注于

cues.en: on building that kind of culture on our teams,
cues.zh: 在团队中建立这种文化，

cues.en: we will do amazing things together.
cues.zh: 我们就能一起成就了不起的事情。

cues.en: Thank you.
cues.zh: 谢谢。
